reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic oscillation with an estimated fundamental period of ~16 points, consistent across all candidates. Each cycle contains a sharp, asymmetric V-shaped trough followed by a slower, convex rise to a broad plateau or gentle peak; the trough is typically 1.0–1.5 standardized units deep and spans ~4–5 points, while the rising limb occupies ~8–10 points and often shows slight curvature (positive second derivative). Amplitude (90th percentile range) varies modestly between 2.07 and 3.17, but shape morphology is highly conserved: troughs are consistently narrow and steep on the left side, smoother on the right; peaks/plateaus are flat-topped or gently rounded, rarely sharp. Baseline level (median) drifts slightly across segments (−0.27 to +0.34), but local stability within each window is high—roughness (~0.202) and curvature (~0.07–0.13) are tightly clustered, indicating low noise and minimal trend within windows. Slope per point is near-zero overall (±0.05), confirming stationarity at the analysis-window scale. Boundary truncation is present in candidate 0 (only 1 cycle), but its morphology matches the first half of longer cycles. No abrupt discontinuities or irregular spikes appear in any candidate; noise appears as small linear interpolation artifacts rather than stochastic jitter. Acceptable variation includes minor shifts in trough depth, plateau width, and exact peak height—but the core V-rise-plateau motif remains invariant.
